description: Who a name in this company's texts is — «Гупта», «N. D. Gupta», «Sjogren». Ask it BEFORE writing a person's name with initials or in another script: the answer is every person the spelling may be, each with all their spellings by script ('latin', 'cyrillic') and form ('full' — with initials or a first name, 'surname', 'inflected' — a declined form), each spelling with the source it was read from and the words there, and 'checked': 'checked' (the quote stands in its source), 'unchecked' (nobody gave a source — somebody remembered it) or 'stale' (the quote stood in its source and was edited out of it, or the source is gone: the spelling may still be right, its proof is not). Write the name as found — «Гупта (N. D. Gupta)» — and never complete initials from memory. 'ambiguous' is true when more than one person is written exactly so (two Guptas): then say which one you mean, or ask. Nothing found: add what you know with set_person, with the source and quote you read it in. Matches any spelling, case aside, then spellings that begin so. Only confirmed persons, and only spellings whose source you may open. Only where the company's plan includes AI.

project.description: A project key to look in it and its parent projects only. Leave out for every project you can read.

spelling.description: The name as you met it, e.g. 'Гупта' or 'N. D. Gupta'.
